title: MQTT Broker and Home Assistant API Testing
goal: Test MQTT brokers for unauthenticated access and topic enumeration, and check Home Assistant instances for API token exposure, unprotected REST API, and default configuration weaknesses.
scope: Create workers/runners/smart_home/runner.py with two test modules: (1) MQTT TESTING: connect to port 1883 (and 8883 for TLS) without credentials. If connection succeeds, subscribe to # (all topics) and listen for 30 seconds. Create CRITICAL finding: 'MQTT broker accepts anonymous connections'. Log sample topic names found (redacted values). Also check for retained messages on common sensitive topics: homeassistant/+/+/state, home/+/+, devices/+. Check port 9001 for MQTT over WebSocket. (2) HOME ASSISTANT TESTING: check port 8123 for Home Assistant. Test: (a) GET /api/ without Authorization header — if returns 200 with data, CRITICAL finding 'Home Assistant API accessible without authentication'. (b) GET /api/config — reveals installed integrations and configuration. (c) Check for long-lived access tokens in common locations. (d) GET /frontend_latest/index.html without auth — if accessible, MEDIUM finding. (e) Check if Supervisor API (port 4357) is accessible. Create findings for: unauthenticated API access, exposed integrations list, accessible configuration details. Add profile passive-lan-smart-home-audit: checks MQTT + Home Assistant + other smart home hubs (OpenHAB port 8080, Domoticz port 8080, Node-RED port 1880).
generation_reason: Home Assistant (port 8123) and MQTT brokers (port 1883) are present in the user's network. MQTT with anonymous access exposes ALL smart home device states, commands, and potentially sensitive data. Home Assistant without authentication gives complete smart home control. Neither is currently tested.
